findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact merge algorithm for `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` layering of structured class-slot keys (e.g., shallow top-level key wins, or deep merge of nested dicts, or: array-of-tables keys are replace-not-merge), and whether `read_reserved_section`'s existing shallow merge is extended or replaced.
evidence: Plan: 'It layers rather than replaces so an environment overriding one key does not have to restate the whole config.'
Plan config example: `[[tool.rebar.llm.trivial.fallback]]` — a nested array-of-tables.
src/rebar/config.py:598-600: `merged.update(sub)` — shallow dict merge, last writer wins at the top level only.
ABSENCE: no deep-merge algorithm, no per-key override rule, no specification of what 'per-key' means for array-typed values.
findings.finding: The `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` per-key layering algorithm is unspecified for structured/array keys. The plan says the file 'layers per-key over the discovered config,' but the existing `read_reserved_section` (the only discovery mechanism) uses `merged.update(sub)` — a shallow dict merge. A class slot's fallback chain is expressed as `[[tool.rebar.llm.trivial.fallback]]`, an array-of-tables inside the `trivial` sub-dict. A shallow update would replace the entire `trivial` dict (clobbering the fallback array) rather than merging the `fallback` key within it. The plan never specifies whether layering is shallow, deep, or key-selective for nested structures.
findings.location: Approach section ('REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE names a file that LAYERS per-key over the discovered config'); Config shape section (fallback array example); src/rebar/config.py:588-601 (read_reserved_section shallow merge)
scenarios: Operator places `[tool.rebar.llm.trivial]` with a fallback chain in REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE; the project pyproject.toml also has `[tool.rebar.llm.trivial]`. The shallow merge replaces the entire trivial sub-dict, silently dropping whichever source loses, contrary to the 'layers per-key' promise.
An executor implementing the layering guesses 'deep merge' while the config system uses shallow, causing subtle provider misconfiguration.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (in the ADR or Scope section) the three known FallbackModel constraints — streaming-only exception-based fallback, provider SDK retry interference, and UnexpectedModelBehavior non-interception — and specify whether rebar's call sites will use streaming mode and whether provider SDK retries will be disabled for FallbackModel-backed classes.
evidence: Plan states: 'pydantic-ai supplies the runtime half … rebar constructs one per class from config' without qualification on streaming or SDK retry interactions.

pydantic-ai docs (ai.pydantic.dev/models/overview/): 'Response-based fallback currently only works with non-streaming requests (agent.run() and agent.run_sync()). For streaming requests (agent.run_stream()), only exception-based fallback is supported.'
pydantic-ai docs: 'When using FallbackModel, it's recommended to disable provider SDK retries to ensure immediate fallback, for example by setting max_retries=0 on a custom OpenAI client.'

GitHub issue #3267: provider SDKs with built-in retry logic 'can significantly delay or prevent the fallback model from being triggered' — rate-limit errors (429) 'would retry for up to 60 seconds before the fallback activated'.
GitHub issue #2837: FallbackModel does not handle UnexpectedModelBehavior raised during response handling (parsing/validation stage), which is relevant to rebar's verifier paths.
findings.finding: The plan's reliance on pydantic-ai FallbackModel as the per-class fallback mechanism does not acknowledge two documented constraints: (1) response-based fallback is silently skipped for streaming requests, and (2) provider SDK built-in retry loops can delay or prevent fallback activation for potentially 60+ seconds.
findings.location: Approach section — 'per-class fallback chains constructed as pydantic-ai FallbackModel'; Scope — 'src/rebar/llm/ — per-class fallback chains constructed as pydantic-ai FallbackModel'
scenarios: If any gate pass uses streaming (agent.run_stream), a response-based fallback_on handler in FallbackModel will silently not trigger, leaving the operator with no fallback even though one is configured.

On a Bedrock or Anthropic provider with SDK-level retries enabled, a rate-limited primary model will block for up to ~60 s before FallbackModel tries the next class entry — defeating the reliability goal.
A verifier path that gets an unparseable structured response (UnexpectedModelBehavior) will surface an error rather than falling over to the next model, even with FallbackModel configured.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the Approach/Scope section: 'All call sites that use a FallbackModel-backed class MUST use non-streaming invocation (agent.run / agent.run_sync) if response-based fallback is required; provider SDK retries (e.g., Anthropic/OpenAI max_retries) MUST be set to 0 on those clients. If streaming is needed for a pass, only exception-based fallback (ModelAPIError) is available.' Capture this as a constraint in the ADR.

The class resolver in `src/rebar/llm/config.py` and any YAML consumer need a closed vocabulary to raise an actionable error rather than silently producing a broken model.

findings.finding: The `fallback_on` trigger conditions for the per-class `FallbackModel` chains are never specified. The plan states 'rebar constructs one per class from config' as `FallbackModel(default, *fallbacks, fallback_on=...)` but leaves the trigger vocabulary (which exception types or response conditions cause fallback) entirely undefined. pydantic-ai's `FallbackModel` has specific semantics for when it delegates to the next model; without specifying `fallback_on`, the executor must guess whether to use pydantic-ai's defaults, rate-limit errors only, or any model exception.
